findings.reason: The protected Python solution determines if two binary addition expression trees are equivalent by comparing leaf variable multiplicities. It traverses root1 adding 1 to a frequency map for each variable leaf and root2 subtracting 1 for each variable leaf, then checks if all net counts are zero. The solution runs in O(n1 + n2) time and O(h + u) space; no candidate is required.
Addition associativity and commutativity allow expressions to be reduced to variable multiset counts. Comparing signed net frequencies verifies whether variable multiplicities match identically.

Traversing both trees takes O(n1 + n2) time. Recursion stack takes O(h) space and frequency map stores u unique variables (u <= 26), giving O(h + u) auxiliary space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts root1 and root2 Node roots, returning boolean true if expression trees are equivalent and false otherwise.

The approach accurately details algebraic leaf frequency counting, signed balance accumulation, zero-balance validation, and O(n1 + n2) time / O(h + u) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover leaf sorting overhead, linear search list removal quadratic costs, structural node-by-node comparison pitfalls, single leaf tree comparisons, variable multiplicity vs set equality, regrouped/reordered equivalent expressions, and internal '+' node exclusions.
